quiz_breakdown.rule: 1 = right and sure; 0.5 = right but unsure; partly answered = answered fraction x (1 if sure, 0.5 if unsure)
quiz_breakdown.remark: Q2, Q6 and Q9 are right by the key but were marked unsure, because the reader computed the answer (cell_at line, 6 of 187, 37 tiles / 33 boxes) instead of reading it. With full credit for derived-and-correct answers the score is 12.33 of 16 (0.77). Q12 misses the next stop, Q15 the guest rule, Q16 the fault-and-fix claim: those three were cut from L2, not misread.

invented: CA_Introduction's board 'steps through the same four rules' (30, 90, 110, 250). Wrong: its buttons are 30, 90, 110 and 184, and it stands at 90.

[worked by hand] Rule 30 drops the walker at row 2's middle hole. Wrong: the autopilot climbed six rows to 0.90 m and fell under row 7. It also contradicts the unfolder's own reading in 13.6, that a 0.6 m walker cannot fall into a 0.4 m hole.
Rule 110 'is the only one the walker can climb'. Wrong: the original walks Sierpinski's rows by their edge to row 8, feet at 1.46 m.

The walker stops on the seed because 'with nothing under its centre it does not step forward', its width keeping it from falling in. This mechanism is invented, and it runs opposite to the original's 'the walker does not fit between them'.
'Cell at 0.2 m makes every gap half as wide compared with the walker's body.' The original sizes the cell against the marble ('smaller than the marble is wide') and drops the marble again.
'Press Play' for diffusion.tscn. The original insists on F6, because Play runs the project's main scene.
GUESTS 'names the guest folders to load', and the stair stands 'at the place you assign it'. In the original, GUESTS takes a .tscn path in room.gd, and the room itself reports place 2.

The process strip 'keeps the mistake... the fault and its fix are both part of how the body was made'. This is an interpretation; the original's claim is that in the picture the fault and the fix are the same size (14.51% and 13.26%).

Rule 30 'orderly on one side, disordered on the other' and Rule 110 'piles up on the left'. These are guesses, in the right direction, for what the original gives as counts (32/30 with 48 cells differing; 33/3, the 3 coming round the ring).

Correct by-hand derivations that the original does not print: row 1 of the one-buffer fault is cells 7-16; ring against dead end is {0,1,15,16} against {1,15} in row 9 and {1,2,14,15} against {0,2,14,16} in row 10; dead-end Rule 90 gives 35 tiles and 35 boxes; the ASCII rows 0-7 of Rule 90; x_of(0) = -3.2 m.

Rule 250 lights a cell when its left or right neighbour is live, Rule 90 when exactly one is: a bit-level reason for 'every tile of Rule 90 is also a tile of Rule 250', which the original asserts but does not derive.
For the walker, 90 and 250 are the same (it stops on both seeds); for the marble they come apart. The original's data supports this synthesis, but the original never says it.

'Two buffers for A and two for B, for the same reason as before: no cell may read a neighbour's answer before it has asked its own question.' This turns the CA_Introduction quote into a general invariant.

Correct elaborations that are not in the original: a line-by-line reaction-diffusion gloss (eaten is the reaction, feed tops A up towards 1, (feed + kill) removes B), the swap as 'three assignments, whatever the size of the row', and cell * 0.9 as a seam between tiles.
A full assembled cellular.gd appendix, marked [guess]. It uses cell_at(i) as the middle term, an if-guard in place of 'while pace <= 0.0 and made < rows', and puts rule fourth among the exports.
An added predict-then-run step in the exercises: 'predict from the binary: 0 answers 0 for everything, 255 answers 1 for everything'.
Provenance markers, [guess] and [worked by hand], on every reconstructed passage.
new_possibilities: Provenance as a type. The unfolder tagged each reconstruction [guess] or [worked by hand]. That is the reader-side twin of the original's honesty line ('Every message and number on this page comes from running the study in Godot 4.6'), which L2 cut. A compressed lesson could tag its claims [measured], [derived], [read from files] or [not watched], so that provenance survives compression as a declared type, not a prose paragraph.

A compression rule from this round trip: cut what is derivable, keep what is measured. Everything derivable from the printed code came back by computation: row 1 = ten cells, 6 border cells, 37 tiles and 33 boxes, the Sierpinski rows. Everything measured in the engine did not: walker heights, the marble, pixel percentages, 2.50 s, 0.420 B, the room walk. The unfolder's errors cluster exactly there (Rule 30's walk, F6, the board's 184). So cut derivable numbers, or turn them into 'compute this' prompts with an answer key, and keep measured numbers, marked [measured], since no future reader can regenerate them.

Derived numbers as exercises. The reader's by-hand counts (6 of 187, 37/33, dead end 35/35) make better practice than the original's printed numbers. A compressed text could ask for them and keep the answers in a key.
The ASCII Rule 90 rows (# for live, . for dead) as a text-only picture. It is cheaper than printed byte arrays and readable by a text-only reader or a screen reader.

The assembled-script appendix as the Stop-here checkpoint, which the original gives only as counts (7 exports, 5 vars, 6 functions). Diffing it against the original also exposed a hidden dependency: 'change the 90 in the first @export line' needs rule to be declared first. Declaration order is part of the type contract, and a compressed version should state it.

A three-measure comparison (eye, marble, walker). 90 and 250 are twins for the eye and for the walker, but not for the marble. That sharpens 'the body measures otherwise' into 'each body measures otherwise'.

The OR-against-XOR reading of the rule bits (250 = left or right, 90 = exactly one) gives a one-line reason for the closest pair. A compressed text can carry a reason like that in place of the assertion.

The CA_Introduction quote generalised into an invariant that covers both the stair and the pool: no cell reads a neighbour's answer before it has asked its own question. That is a candidate definition for the 'two buffers' type.

A self-check for future unfolders. Here 13.6 says the walker's width stops it falling in, while 13.7 drops it through a one-cell hole. An unfolder could reconcile every walk claim against one body model and report each conflict as a stuck point, not resolve it silently.
lost_vectors: Direction, from question to definition. The original opens with a method: 'A lesson starts in its hall, with one question: does the hall show one work at several values of one axis?' L2 makes it a type: 'A family is one work at several values of one @export.' The answer has replaced the question, and 'axis' (what the work argues) has narrowed to '@export' (how it is mounted), the very slip the project's DNA notes warn against.

Force of provenance. Cut: 'Every message and number on this page comes from running the study in Godot 4.6... No headset was used anywhere', 'we did not walk them', 'no hand was on the keys: every walk above was the autopilot's' and 'we did not render that one'. The voice moves from 'we measured' to 'it is'. 'We found out by running them' becomes 'You find out by running them', a report turned into an instruction. 'Both are our decisions; the pattern has no part in them' becomes 'It bears weight through your choices': the decider moves from author to student, and the pattern's having no part is dropped.

Force of prediction. The bold 'Before you run, predict row 1' becomes 'Predict row 1: two cells, a gap between, a mirrored floor', so the prediction is handed over as an answer. 'Write your prediction before you render... Will those two pairs be equally alike?' loses both its deadline and its question, and the unfolder then reads the two-answers fact as 'a clue', the opposite of its role.

Force of making error ordinary. 'Godot printed nothing else: no error, no warning. The code ran exactly as written, and reading a result like this one is ordinary work' becomes 'No error: the code ran as written.' The ordinariness, the emotional ground of the closing habit, is gone, and the unfolder fills the gap with blame ('so the mistake is in what was written').

Force of scope and evidence. Cut: 'Our sheet is eleven rows from one seed. We counted two other floors... and the pair stayed the closest', the four-rule ring/dead-end counts (2, 6, 3, 4), the second pool run that 'held the same numbers, to the last digit', and Rule 30's middle column read twice. The claims survive bare, without hedge or evidence: 'Rule 30 looks random and holds no chance' now rests on nothing.

Connection to the halls. The museum dialogue collapses. The CA_Introduction quote survives without its source and reads as the lesson's epigraph. Cut entirely: CA_EdgeOfChaos ('Every cell reads the previous volume'), the hall's ring line ('What looks like a line on the desk is a ring to the calculation'), the Reaction_Diffusion_Systems desk with its six feed/kill pairs, the hall footnote behind 'Gray and Scott', and the board's 184, which the unfolder then filled with 250.

Connection to earlier chapters. The pendulum's MultiMesh, the chessboard's index and %, and the seeds chapter shrink to bare 'needs:' tokens. A token declares what is required but not where it was learned, so the unfolder taught MultiMesh as new and guessed 'the randomness chapter'. The type is declared, but its lineage is lost.

Shortcut into system: the guest. 'Its script is the cellular.gd you wrote with its colour written out: a guest may name nothing outside its own folder' becomes 'A guest is a body your room loads from its own folder.' The prohibition became an address, so the reason for the written-out colour vanished, and with it the link between the student's own script and the room it must enter. Also cut: room.gd, the exact res:// line, 'in the room's copy... the first @export line', and the measured arrival at place 2.

Shortcut into system: F6. 'Press F6, which runs the scene that is open instead of the project's main scene' became 'In diffusion.tscn'. The unfolder wrote 'Press Play', the very action the original's explanation guards against.

Shortcut into system: the marble and the walker. 'Make cell smaller than the marble is wide, 0.2 m, and drop it again' lost its 'than the marble', so the unfolder attached the 0.2 m cell to the walker. 'The walker does not fit between them' became '0.4 m; 0.6 m wide', and the unfolder read the width as what saves the walker from falling in, the opposite sense.

Direction of the walk. 'The place this chapter asks for is to stand on the history and walk up Sierpinski's rows' and 'Sierpinski's rows can be walked by their edge... row 8 with its feet at 1.46 m' are both cut. The unfolder concluded that Rule 110 'is the only one the walker can climb', which inverts the chapter's destination: in the original the fractal the eye admires is walkable after all, by its edge.

Direction of scale. 'The course's outline carries a question from its Queer 3D reference into this chapter: can twisted rooms transcend power? We leave it as a question. What the kit shows is smaller' became 'Can twisted rooms transcend power? It stays a question.' Without its source and without the turn to 'smaller', the question floats as rhetoric; the reader 'could not see the point'.

Direction onward, and what a picture cannot see. Cut: 'The next stop, The tree and its mad branch, keeps the idea of a rule applied to its own result and drops the grid', so the chapter no longer points on. Also cut: 'in the picture the fault and the fix are the same size' (14.51% and 13.26%), the strip's claim that a still cannot tell an error from its repair; and 'Either is right', the permission inside Decide.
readability: Lighter on the page (2,389 words against 5,477) and easy where the code carries the meaning: the reader rebuilt 13.2-13.4 and 13.8, worked out 10 cells, 6 border cells and 37/33 by hand, and got every code question right, although three of those answers were marked unsure only because the number was derived, not stated. Hard where a line points at the world without its referent (Import the study, Look, the halls, the marble, sheet.gd, GUESTS, place 2, 'by weight / by arrangement', the Queer 3D question) or gives code only in words (lay_row in 13.3, the cell_at line in 13.5, the guard in 13.6): 23 stuck points and a 5,987-word unfolding show that the load moved from reading to inferring more than it shrank.
